answer:
Set up a 2D dam-break case in OpenFOAM using the interFoam solver.
The computational domain is 10 m in x, 5 m in y, and 1 cell in z, defined in system/blockMeshDict.
Use a uniform hexahedral mesh of 100 cells in x, 50 cells in y, and 1 cell in z, giving 0.1 m cell spacing.
Set the frontAndBack boundary patch to type empty in blockMeshDict.
Set the bottom, left (x=0), right (x=10), and top (y=5) boundary patches to type wall in blockMeshDict.
In system/controlDict, set the application to interFoam.
In system/controlDict, set the simulation end time to 2 seconds, with a time step of 0.001 seconds.
In system/fvSchemes, use upwind for geometric and non-geometric surface gradients, linear for volume gradients, and MULES for the alpha transport scheme.
In system/fvSolution, use PIMPLE with 2 corrector iterations, and set the relaxation factor for U to 0.3.
Initialize alpha.water to 1 inside the box from (0,0,0) to (5,2.5,1) and 0 everywhere else using a setFieldsDict with a boxToCell region.
In constant/physicalProperties, set water density to 1000 kg/m3, water dynamic viscosity to 1e-3 Pa.s, air density to 1.2 kg/m3, and air dynamic viscosity to 1.8e-5 Pa.s.
In constant/g, set the gravitational acceleration to (0 -9.81 0).
Set all wall boundary conditions for U to noSlip, for p to zeroGradient, and for alpha.water to zeroGradient.
Set the frontAndBack boundary conditions for all fields to empty.
The water column occupies x from 0 to 5 m and y from 0 to 2.5 m, sitting on the bottom wall, with air filling the remainder of the domain.
